page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4mds_v2 is a constrained-core virtual machine instance configured with an asymmetric resource profile. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Although based on an FX16 chassis, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. This x86_64 CPU configuration includes advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8, accompanied by a 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, provisioning 336.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 84.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed locally via 944 GB of NVMe SSD space. The server does not include dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant contrast between single-thread frequency and overall aggregate throughput. The high 4.2 GHz core frequency drives top-tier single-core compute, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 2357.0 (top 10%) and strong throughput in single-threaded compression tests like gzip (34.85 GB/sec) and bzip3 (14.39 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded compute is constrained by the 4-vCPU allocation, as reflected in lower-tier stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded decompression metrics. Memory operations show fast cached bandwidth (345.84 GB/sec at 16 KB) but drop to 36.33 GB/sec on uncached large-block read operations. LLM text generation scaling degrades significantly under larger 7B and 70B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX16-4mds_v2 is engineered for software architectures bound by per-core licensing models that still demand heavy memory capacity and local NVMe caching. By offering 336.0 GB of RAM alongside 4 licensed vCPUs, it circumvents expensive multi-socket licensing overhead while maintaining access to large working datasets. However, for compute-heavy parallel workloads, the core limitation represents a performance tradeoff relative to the underlying chassis size.

Appropriate workload fits for the Azure FX16-4mds_v2 include in-memory databases, memory-intensive relational database engines, EDA (Electronic Design Automation) simulation tools requiring high single-core clocks, and caching layers like Redis (which achieved 6.34 million operations/sec) that operate best within extreme RAM-to-core ratios.

Driven by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor on the x86_64 architecture, the server pairs 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores) with an extensive 336.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 84.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage needs are served by 944 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, without GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-core efficiency, marked by high single-threaded compression rates and a Geekbench single-core score of 2357.0, offset by multi-core constraints due to the 4-thread envelope. Delivering balanced Redis throughput and solid database operations, this instance is suited for in-memory databases, caching deployments, and memory-intensive applications requiring high clock frequencies on limited licensed cores.
